name: Bite-edge exposure to vertical spinner
mechanism: A tooth needs a horizontal-ish edge or step to catch; any step >= tooth bite depth lets it transfer full energy instead of glancing.
measure: Ray-cast from front/side bands (z 0-40 mm, elevation -10..+30 deg, 2 deg az x 1 mm z grid) onto hull; at each hit, compute surface normal; flag faces whose normal has a component opposing the ray >cos(30deg) AND that form a step (adjacent face height jump) >= bite depth. Bite depth d = v_closing / (n_teeth * rpm/60) (e.g. 3 m/s, 2 teeth, 15000 rpm -> 6 mm).
threshold: no exposed step >= 0.5*d on front/side faces; sloped (>=35 deg from vertical) faces count as glancing
fix: Remove vertical steps, chamfer edges >= bite depth, slope front faces back >= 35 deg, hide screw heads below surface.
countermeasure: sloped armour, smooth hull, recessed fasteners

name: Front lip survives a vertical-spinner hit
mechanism: Thin wedge/fork tips meet the teeth first; a printed or 0.8 mm lip shatters or bends up, leaving a gap the spinner then exploits.
measure: Model lip as cantilever plate: width b, thickness t, overhang L. Absorbed energy capacity U = (sigma_y^2/(2E))*vol for elastic + plastic term for metals; for FDM use Charpy-like energy density from material table (PLA 2-4 kJ/m2, PETG 4-8, TPU no-break, Ti 6Al4V high). Compare to E_hit = 0.5*E_tip (half energy transferred on glancing).
threshold: U_capacity >= 0.5*E_tip_ref (25 J) for metal lips; printed lips must be TPU or backed by metal
fix: Use 0.8-1.5 mm hardened steel or Ti lip, or TPU-flex fork; shorten overhang.

name: Forks vs spinner (sacrificial spacing)
mechanism: Forks present less bite; if tine gaps are wider than tooth width they still let the disc reach the body, but they should break off before the chassis.
measure: Tine gap g vs ref tooth width (6-12 mm); tine mounting bolt shear load at E_tip impulse.
threshold: g <= 8 mm or solid lip; tine fixings weaker than chassis (failsafe) => info if not
fix: Make tines replaceable with shear-able fixings; keep gaps < tooth width.

name: Launch arm: CG height vs contact point
mechanism: Hit below CG flips/launches robot; impulse J = sqrt(2*m_opp_weapon_I*E)/r. Rotational launch more likely when contact far below CG.
measure: Contact height h_c (lowest exposed front point that spinner reaches, from R050 sweep of a ref 60 mm disc at 5 mm ground clearance) and CG height z_cg; launch angular impulse = J*(z_cg-h_c). Compute post-hit vertical velocity v_z = J/m, flight apex = v_z^2/2g.
threshold: apex <= 100 mm advisory info; >= 300 mm warning (landing damage CF-LD*)
fix: Lower CG, use full-floor lip so contact is low and glancing.

name: Top edge catch for drum
mechanism: Drums hit the top front edge of tall robots; vertical face above the lip is a catch.
measure: Ray grid from front at drum height band z 15-45 mm; find faces with normal within 30 deg of -ray; area fraction of front silhouette.
threshold: exposed vertical front area < 15% of front silhouette
fix: Make front a continuous slope from lip to top; reduce height.

name: Gyro of own vertical weapon on hit (stall/reaction)
mechanism: Opposite reaction torque on hit pitches robot; if weapon motor mount or belt slips, weapon dead.
measure: Reaction impulse = E_own/(r_tip*omega) ; check motor mount bolt shear and frame bending at weapon uprights using strength.upright loads multiplied by 2 (dynamic factor).
threshold: SF >= 2 on uprights; mount bolts M2+ x2 per side
fix: Thicken uprights, add a crossbar, use through-bolt axle.

name: Side armour bite by horizontal spinner
mechanism: Undercutters hit 0-15 mm high at the side; vertical side walls give full bite.
measure: Ray casts horizontally at z 2-15 mm from 360 deg; fraction of side perimeter where the hit face is vertical (+/-15 deg) and unshielded by a skirt that extends >= 3 mm outboard.
threshold: < 30% of side perimeter vertical-and-exposed at z<15
fix: Add angled side skirts or wedgelets, flexible acetate skirts.

name: Wheel exposure to horizontal blade
mechanism: A wheel touched by an undercutter is torn off or stalls the drive.
measure: Ray casts at wheel centre height from 360 deg; any ray hitting a wheel before a static part.
threshold: 0 exposed rays outside +/-20 deg of the rear (warning), wheel exposed at front/side band -> warning
fix: Recess wheels inside body walls; add guard plates outboard.

name: Overcutter top exposure
mechanism: Bar at 30-60 mm clears low wedges and hits tops; protruding top features (switches, weapon pulleys) get ripped.
measure: Height map of top surface; list features above z_top-5 mm within reach; check what component they belong to.
threshold: no critical component (switch, receiver, belt) in top 5 mm

name: Being launched sideways (recoil spin-out)
mechanism: Hit imparts lateral impulse; if traction low robot spins out and the side wall then gets hit.
measure: Lateral impulse J vs friction*m*g*t_contact; yaw inertia from mass props.
threshold: info only: report predicted yaw rate
fix: Increase yaw inertia via wide track; low CG.

name: Skirt edge lift into undercutter
mechanism: A flexible skirt rising >3 mm gives the blade an edge.
measure: Hinged/flexible skirt lip rest height after compression of tyres (R077) and max deflection under 2 N.
threshold: lip <= 1 mm under 2 N upward
fix: Stiffen skirt or add weight; use spring steel.

name: Top plate penetration by axe
mechanism: Pointed axe tip punches printed top plates; damage lands on internals underneath.
measure: For each top hit-point grid cell: plate thickness t (ray thickness z), span to nearest support (distance to nearest wall in XY), punch shear capacity F = tau*pi*d_tip*t (d_tip 3 mm) and plate bending energy. Compare to E_hammer=5 J.
threshold: punch energy capacity >= 5 J over critical components; else warning
fix: Thicker top over electronics, 0.5 mm Ti or polycarbonate lid, ribs to cut span.

name: Critical part directly under thin top
mechanism: Damage path from top: what is within 10 mm below a thin region.
measure: Vertical rays down from top grid; first internal component hit within 10 mm of plate underside.
threshold: receiver/ESC/battery not under any cell with capacity < 5 J
fix: Move electronics under ribs or add standoff.

name: Hammer-saw / top saw abrasion of wires
mechanism: Saw dwells on top; any wire within top 3 mm cut.
measure: Wire paths (wiring.route) min distance to top outer surface.
threshold: > 4 mm

name: Get-under margin vs reference opponents
mechanism: Whoever is lower wins; compare edge gap distribution to reference opponents from taxonomy.
measure: Per bearing edge gap (combat R-series) vs taxonomy reference lip heights (0.0-0.5 mm metal, fork tips 0.2); win fraction = share of bearings where ours <= theirs.
threshold: front win fraction >= 0.7 vs median reference
fix: Lower lip, metal edge, hinged skirt.

name: Lift torque needed (resistance to being lifted)
mechanism: A lifter must raise CG; heavy front & low CG increase required lift work.
measure: Lift work W = m*g*delta_z_cg when pivoting on rear edge to 45 deg; tipping torque at front lip.
threshold: info: report W; warning if CG > 60% of length toward rear (easy to pry from front)
fix: Move mass forward, keep CG low.

name: Grab points for grabbers/crushers
mechanism: Grabbers need a gripable section; overhangs and narrow waists help them.
measure: Search for horizontal widths < 60 mm with undercut (concave) profiles in side sections.
threshold: no concave pockets > 5 mm deep on sides/top

name: Crusher clamp load on shell
mechanism: Clamp crushes printed shell onto battery.
measure: Compress shell between plates: crushing force capacity via plate buckling/bending at shell walls; distance shell inner to battery.
threshold: shell deflection at 200 N < gap to battery

name: Flip landing recovery
mechanism: Once flipped you must work inverted.
measure: Reuse R090-R093 plus CF-LD.
threshold: see R090

name: Wedge-on-wedge stalemate push
mechanism: When both are equal, pushing force decides.
measure: Max traction push = mu*m_on_driven*g vs motor stall force at wheel radius.
threshold: push >= 1.3 N per 100 g

name: Side approach / T-bone get-under
mechanism: Sides usually higher than front.
measure: Side edge gap median vs front.
threshold: side median gap <= front + 1 mm

group: E. Arena, hazards, pits, walls, inverted, landing
name: Wall pinning
mechanism: Robot pinned with weapon side to wall loses mobility.
measure: Footprint shape: can it rotate when one side is against a flat wall (wheel touches wall?).
threshold: wheels not first contact with a wall from any side

group: E. Arena, hazards, pits, walls, inverted, landing
name: Pit/out-of-arena drift
mechanism: Low traction or slow robot is pushed out.
measure: Push resistance and speed (R074, R124).
threshold: see refs

group: E. Arena, hazards, pits, walls, inverted, landing
name: Stuck on the side
mechanism: Robot resting on side cannot recover.
measure: Stable rest poses from convex hull; if any rest pose has no wheel ground contact and no self-right -> warning.
threshold: no trapped rest pose other than inverted with wheels touching

group: E. Arena, hazards, pits, walls, inverted, landing
name: Landing impact on printed chassis
mechanism: Drop energy m*g*h = 0.15*9.81*1 = 1.5 J concentrates on corners.
measure: Drop test: for each convex-hull vertex as landing point, local corner wall thickness and layer orientation; capacity via energy density of material.
threshold: capacity >= 1.5 J at all corners

group: E. Arena, hazards, pits, walls, inverted, landing
name: Landing on wheels/shaft
mechanism: Landing on a wheel bends a 3 mm shaft or N20 output.
measure: Shaft bending stress from F = m*g*n (n=20 g decel) at overhang length.

group: E. Arena, hazards, pits, walls, inverted, landing
name: Component ejection on landing
mechanism: Loose battery/receiver moves and rips connectors.
measure: Each component must have retention: contact faces on >= 4 of 6 directions (internal.no_contact) or strap.
threshold: all heavy parts constrained in 6 directions

name: Wheel-to-guard gap jam band
mechanism: Debris wedges between rotating tyre and static guard and stalls the wheel.
measure: Min distance from wheel/tyre swept volume (revolve wheel) to nearest static part; histogram per angular sector.
threshold: gap in 1.5-15 mm open band where debris can enter -> warning; <1.5 mm (tight) or >15 mm (falls through) OK
fix: Close gap to <1.5 mm with a scraper or open to >15 mm.

name: Weapon-to-frame jam band
mechanism: Debris caught between spinning weapon and frame stops it or breaks belt.
measure: Weapon swept volume vs static parts min gap per sector.
threshold: no 1.5-10 mm gaps below the weapon axis

name: Belt/pulley pinch point exposure
mechanism: Debris into belt nip throws belt.
measure: Find belt entry nip (tangent points) and check line-of-sight from outside (ray casts from exterior) within 15 mm.
threshold: nips enclosed (no exterior ray)

name: Open vents/holes admitting debris
mechanism: Holes >2 mm over electronics let shards in.
measure: Holes in shell (boundary loops) with diameter > 2 mm above/near electronics.
threshold: none above electronics

name: Exposed gearbox/motor shaft
mechanism: N20 output exposed gets debris in gears.
measure: Ray-visibility of gearbox from outside.
threshold: info if visible

name: Tyre debris trap (treads)
mechanism: Tyre grooves 2-4 mm pack with dust.
measure: Tyre profile grooves width.
threshold: info

name: Layer-direction weakness at hit points
mechanism: FDM inter-layer strength ~ 30-60% of in-plane; hits loading layers in tension delaminate.
measure: For each hit point: print orientation from spec (build direction); stress direction = normal of impact; if principal bending tension is along build Z, apply knockdown 0.4.
threshold: SF after knockdown >= 1.5
fix: Re-orient print so layers run along impact face.

name: Thin wall at hit point
mechanism: Wall thickness < 2 mm fails on any spinner hit.
measure: Ray thickness along inward normal at grid point.
threshold: t >= 2.5 mm printed / >= 0.8 mm metal at exposed faces

name: Stress concentration at sharp internal corners
mechanism: Sharp internal corners crack.
measure: Detect concave edges with dihedral angle < 120 deg and radius < 0.5 mm in shell.
threshold: fillets >= 1 mm

name: Bolt boss pull-out under hit
mechanism: Bosses in PLA tear out.
measure: Existing strength.bolt_pullout at dynamic factor 3.

name: Brittle material on impact face
mechanism: PLA shatters; TPU/PETG/Nylon absorb.
measure: Material of each exposed part from spec vs brittle list.
threshold: no PLA on front/side exposed faces

name: Global frame torsion / split
mechanism: Hits split the chassis at narrow cross-sections.
measure: Slice chassis at 2 mm intervals along X and Y; min section modulus; compare to M = J*v/... -> simplified M = F_peak*L with F_peak = E/delta (delta 2 mm).
threshold: SF >= 1

group: H. Graceful degradation and internal placement
name: Chunk-removal survivability
mechanism: Remove 20 mm sphere at each hit-point; check if drive, weapon, power and radio subgraph remain connected.
measure: Build connectivity graph: components (battery, ESC, receiver, motors, switch) + wires as edges with paths; for each hit point remove components/wires intersecting the sphere; check robot still drives at least one side and has power.
threshold: drive alive in >= 80% of front/side hit points
fix: Move parts deeper, reroute wires, redundant links.

group: H. Graceful degradation and internal placement
name: Single-point-of-failure wire
mechanism: One wire supplying everything near the skin.
measure: Min distance of battery main lead / power bus to outer surface.
threshold: > 8 mm

group: H. Graceful degradation and internal placement
name: Battery near impact face
mechanism: LiPo puncture -> fire / disqualification.
measure: Distance from battery to front/side/top outer skin along impact rays; penetration estimate from impact map.
threshold: > 10 mm and not in damage map

group: H. Graceful degradation and internal placement
name: Receiver/antenna exposure
mechanism: Receiver damage = dead robot; antenna cut = failsafe.
measure: Receiver distance to skin; antenna path within metal enclosure?
threshold: receiver > 8 mm from skin; antenna not enclosed in full metal
fix: Move receiver; route antenna out of metal box.

group: H. Graceful degradation and internal placement
name: Drive redundancy
mechanism: 2WD with one wheel lost is crippled; 4WD survives.
measure: Count independent drive motors per side; check each side has wheels that survive chunk removal at any single hit.
threshold: info

group: H. Graceful degradation and internal placement
name: Switch/link accessibility and protection
mechanism: Removable link needed per rules; exposed switch may switch off when hit.
measure: Switch within top/side skin but recessed > 1 mm; not in front band.
threshold: recessed and not in front 30% length

group: H. Graceful degradation and internal placement
name: Connector strain relief
mechanism: Shock tears unrelieved solder joints.
measure: Each wire end has bend/loop slack length >= 5 mm (wiring.bend).
threshold: yes

group: H. Graceful degradation and internal placement
name: Weapon motor wires near spinning parts
mechanism: Wire touching weapon is cut.
measure: Distance wire path to weapon swept volume.
threshold: > 3 mm

group: H. Graceful degradation and internal placement
name: ESC thermal/mechanical isolation
mechanism: ESC boards crack under shock.
measure: ESC contacts hard frame without foam?
threshold: info

group: I. Arena surface: wood floor wear, seams, wall gap, screws, pits
name: Splinter/gouge snag vs fork tip angle
attacker: worn wooden floor (raised splinters 0.3-1.5 mm, gouges)
mechanism: A tip that meets a raised splinter at a steep angle hooks it and stops/pivots the robot; a shallow tip rides over. Trade-off: lower tip wins the under race but meets more splinters.
measure: Tip attack angle alpha = angle between the bottom face of each tine/lip within 3 mm of the leading edge and the floor (from section at each tine centreline). Ride-over condition for a splinter of height h: tan(alpha) < mu_wood(0.4)... use alpha <= 20 deg and tip radius r >= h_splinter/2.
threshold: alpha 10-20 deg and tip radius 0.3-1.0 mm: OK; alpha > 30 deg or r < 0.1 mm (knife edge into floor): warning
fix: Rake the underside of tines up 10-15 deg in the last 3 mm; radius the tip 0.3-0.5 mm; keep top-face sharp for bite.

group: I. Arena surface: wood floor wear, seams, wall gap, screws, pits
name: Floor-panel seam/step catch
attacker: seams and 0.5-2 mm steps between floor panels
mechanism: Lip at 0.2 mm meets a 1 mm step head-on and stops dead (or pivots if only one side catches). Trade-off: lip below step height maximises get-under but guarantees seam strikes.
measure: Leading-edge rake beta (angle of the lip's front-bottom chamfer) and step-climb: lip climbs if the contact normal points upward: step h, tip radius r, rake beta -> climbs if h < r*(1-cos(90-beta)) + chamfer height. Compute chamfer height c from section (vertical extent of the bottom chamfer).
threshold: chamfer/radius height c >= 1 mm OR lip hinged (R035/R036): OK; rigid lip with c < 0.5 mm at <= 0.5 mm height: warning
fix: Add 1 mm x 30 deg under-chamfer to the lip or hinge it so it rides up seams.

group: I. Arena surface: wood floor wear, seams, wall gap, screws, pits
name: Lip stiffness vs dig-in
mechanism: A very stiff lip pressed down by robot weight/opponent digs into soft wood; a too-flexible lip folds under. Trade-off: stiff = consistent low edge, but digs; flexible = conforms, but folds or lifts.
measure: Lip tip vertical stiffness k = 3EI/L^3 (per mm width) from section; contact pressure at tip under robot weight share W_lip (from statics: CG vs wheels vs lip contact) p = W_lip/(tip contact area = width*2r).
threshold: p < 5 MPa (soft pine indentation ~ 5-10 MPa) and k in 0.5-5 N/mm per tine/strip
fix: Increase tip radius / contact width, carry weight on wheels not lip, choose spring steel 0.3-0.5 mm.

group: I. Arena surface: wood floor wear, seams, wall gap, screws, pits
name: Flexible tine wedging into floor-wall gap
mechanism: Narrow flexible tines enter the gap under/beside the wall and jam; robot is self-pinned. Trade-off: thin, narrow, flexible tines are best at getting under and worst for this.
measure: Min tine/lip feature width w_min (from front-section slicing at z=0-2 mm), tine flex delta under 2 N lateral/down load, tip shape (pointed vs blunt). Risk if w_min within gap band [2,6] mm AND tine height < gap AND delta > 0.5 mm.
threshold: w_min > 8 mm or tine tips joined by crossbar or tip radius >= w/2: OK; else warning
fix: Make tines >= 8 mm wide at the tip, join tips, or blunt tips; avoid needle tips.

group: I. Arena surface: wood floor wear, seams, wall gap, screws, pits
name: Snag on arena screws/hazard plates
attacker: raised screw heads (1-3 mm), hazard edges, pit lips
mechanism: Low edges hook raised screws; side skirts snag hazard plates. Trade-off: same as floor seams.
measure: Same climb test as CF-AS02 with h = 3 mm across front and side skirts; side skirts additionally need side-chamfer.
threshold: side skirt lower edges chamfered >= 30 deg
fix: Chamfer all skirt bottom edges, not just front.

group: I. Arena surface: wood floor wear, seams, wall gap, screws, pits
name: Pit-edge hang-up
mechanism: Long overhanging forks bridge a pit edge and lever robot in, or hang it. Trade-off: long forks reach under further.
measure: Fork overhang beyond front wheel axle vs wheelbase; CG lever: if overhang > 0.5*wheelbase and CG forward of front wheel contact when front fork unsupported.
threshold: overhang <= 0.5 wheelbase

group: I. Arena surface: wood floor wear, seams, wall gap, screws, pits
name: Asymmetric snag pivot
mechanism: Single tine snagging makes robot spin, presenting its side. Trade-off: multiple independent tines = more snag points.
measure: Tine count and spacing; independent tines without crossbar and spacing > 30 mm -> pivot torque arm.
threshold: info
fix: Link tines or keep them close to centreline.

group: I. Arena surface: wood floor wear, seams, wall gap, screws, pits
name: Floor wear rounding over time
mechanism: Lip wear rounds the edge raising effective height after 2-3 fights. Trade-off: soft lips conform but wear.
measure: Lip material hardness; printed lips predicted to wear 0.2-0.5 mm per fight.
threshold: metal or replaceable lip

name: Weapon self-damage on floor strike when hopping
mechanism: Hop on hit lowers weapon into the floor.
measure: Weapon min clearance at max pitch 5 deg forward.
threshold: > 0 mm
fix: Raise weapon or limit pitch with skirt.

name: Gyro bounce onto back while turning
mechanism: Gyro torque lifts one side on turns.
measure: R057 quantify vs wheel grip.
threshold: see R057

name: Belt slip/derail on hit
mechanism: Hit shock derails belt.
measure: Belt wrap angle >= 150 deg, flanges present, tension check.
threshold: flanged pulleys

name: Weapon bearing support after shell damage
mechanism: If an upright is chunked, weapon falls out.
measure: Chunk-removal at each upright: does weapon still have 2 supports.
threshold: info

name: Power-on after inversion (battery shift)
mechanism: Battery shift pulls connector.
measure: see CF-LD03
